verses.text: “You know di time when mountain goats dey born? You dey watch when di doe dey born young one?
You fit count di months wey dem dey complete? Or you know di time when dem dey born?
Dem dey bend down. Dem dey born dem young. Dem dey finish dem labor pains.
Dem young ones dey grow strong. Dem dey grow for di open field. Dem dey go out and no dey return again.
Who don set di wild donkey free? Or who don loosen di ropes of di fast donkey,
wey I don make di wilderness im home and di salt land im dwelling place?
E dey laugh at di noise of di city and no dey hear di shout of di driver.
Di mountains na im pasture. E dey search for every green thing.
Wild ox go gree serve you? Or e go stay by your feeding place?
You fit tie wild ox for di furrow with im harness? Or e go plough di valleys after you?
You go trust am because im strength big? Or you go leave your work to am?
You go depend on am to bring home your seed and gather di grain of your threshing floor?
Di ostrich wings dey flap proudly, but im feathers dey kind?
Because e dey leave im eggs for di ground and dey warm dem for dust,
and e forget say foot fit crush dem or say wild animal fit trample dem.
E dey hard against im young ones as if no be im own. Even though im labor dey for nothing, e no dey fear,
because God don remove wisdom from am and no give am understanding.
When e lift imself up high, e dey laugh at di horse and im rider.
You don give di horse strength? You don cover im neck with shaking mane?
You don make am jump like locust? Di glory of im snort dey fearful.
E dey scratch di ground for di valley and dey rejoice for im strength. E dey go out to meet di armed men.
E dey laugh at fear and no dey shake, and e no dey turn back from di sword.
Di quiver dey rattle against am, di shining spear and di javelin.
E dey eat di ground with fierceness and rage, and e no dey stand still when e hear di sound of di trumpet.
Every time di trumpet sound, e dey snort, ‘Aha!’ E dey smell di battle from far, di thunder of di captains and di shouting.
Na your wisdom make di hawk dey fly up and stretch im wings toward di south?
Na your command make di eagle dey go up and make im nest for high?
E dey stay for di cliff and make im home, for di point of di cliff and di stronghold.
From dere e dey spy out di prey. Im eyes dey see am from far.
Im young ones dey suck blood too. Where di dead dey, na dere e dey.”
Di Lord answer Job again say,
“Di one wey dey argue go fight di Almighty? Di one wey dey argue with God, make e answer am.”
Den Job answer di Lord say,
“Look, I no be anything. Wetin I go answer you? I put my hand for my mouth.
I don talk one time, and I no go answer. Yes, two times, but I no go talk again.”
Den di Lord answer Job out of di whirlwind say,
“Now tie your waist like man. I go ask you, and you go answer me.
You go even cancel my judgment? You go condemn me so dat you go dey right?
Or you get arm like God? You fit thunder with voice like am?
Now decorate yourself with excellence and dignity. Dress yourself with glory and beauty.
Pour out di fury of your anger. Look everybody wey dey proud and bring am low.
Look everybody wey dey proud and make am humble. Crush di wicked for dem place.
Hide dem together for dust. Tie dem faces for di hidden place.
Den I go agree with you too say your own right hand fit save you.
Look behemoth now, wey I make like I make you. E dey eat grass like ox.
Look now, im strength dey im thighs. Im force dey di muscles of im belly.
E dey move im tail like cedar. Di muscles of im thighs dey tied together.
Im bones be like bronze pipes. Im limbs be like iron bars.
E be di chief of God ways. Di one wey make am give am im sword.
Sure sure di mountains dey bring am food, where all di wild animals dey play.
E dey lie under di lotus trees, for di cover of di reed and di swamp.
Di lotus trees cover am with dem shade. Di willows of di stream dey round am.
Look, if river overflow, e no dey shake. E dey confident, even though di Jordan rise reach im mouth.
Anybody fit catch am when e dey watch, or pierce im nose with trap?”
“You fit pull out Leviathan with fishhook or press im tongue down with rope?
You fit put rope inside im nose or pierce im jaw with hook?
E go beg you plenty times or e go talk soft words to you?
E go make covenant with you, so dat you go take am as servant forever?
You go play with am like bird? Or you go tie am for your girls?
Traders go bargain over am? Dem go share am among di merchants?
You fit fill im skin with sharp irons or im head with fish spears?
Put your hand on am. Remember di battle, and never do am again.
Look, hope to catch am na for nothing. Person no go fall down even at di sight of am?
Nobody dey fierce so tay e go dare wake am up. Who den fit stand before me?
Who don give me first, so dat I go pay am back? Everything under all di sky na my own.
I no go keep quiet about im limbs, im mighty strength or im fine body.
Who fit remove im outer cover? Who go enter inside im jaws?
Who fit open di doors of im face? Terror dey round im teeth.
Strong scales na im pride, wey dem lock together like tight seal.
One near another so tay no air fit pass between dem.
Dem join one to another. Dem stick together so dat dem no fit separate.
Im sneezing dey flash light. Im eyes be like di eyelids of di morning.
Burning torches dey come out of im mouth. Sparks of fire dey jump out.
Smoke dey come out of im nose, like boiling pot over fire of reeds.
Im breath dey light coals. Flame dey come out of im mouth.
Strength dey stay for im neck. Terror dey dance before am.
Di folds of im flesh join together. Dem firm on am. Dem no fit move.
Im heart hard like stone, yes, hard like di lower millstone.
When e raise imself up, di mighty dey fear. Because of fright, dem no sabi wetin dem dey do.
If person attack am with sword, e no go work, or spear, dart or pointed arrow.
E count iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
Arrow no fit make am run. Sling stones be like chaff to am.
Clubs dey count as dry grass. E dey laugh at di rushing of di javelin.
Im under parts be like sharp broken pot. E dey spread imself like threshing sledge for mud.
E dey make di deep boil like pot. E dey make di sea like pot of ointment.
E dey make path shine after am. Person go think say di deep get white hair.
For earth nobody dey like am, wey dem make without fear.
E dey see everything wey dey high. E be king over all di sons of pride.”
Den Job answer di Lord say,
“I know say you fit do all things, and say nobody fit stop your plan.
You ask say, ‘Who be dis one wey dey hide advice without knowledge?’ So I don talk wetin I no understand, things wey too wonderful for me, wey I no know.
You talk say, ‘Listen now, and I go talk. I go ask you, and you go answer me.’
I don hear about you with di hearing of di ear, but now my eye don see you.
So I hate myself and I repent for dust and ashes.”

E happen say after di Lord don talk dis words to Job, di Lord talk to Eliphaz di Temanite say, “My anger burn against you and against your two friends, because una no talk di right thing about me, as my servant Job don talk.

So now, take seven bulls and seven rams for una self and go to my servant Job and offer burnt offering for una self. My servant Job go pray for una, because I go accept am, so dat I no go do to una according to una foolishness. Because una no talk di right thing about me, as my servant Job don talk.”
So Eliphaz di Temanite, Bildad di Shuhite and Zophar di Naamathite go and do wetin di Lord command dem, and di Lord accept Job.
Di Lord bring back Job from im trouble when e pray for im friends. Di Lord give Job twice as much as e get before.

Den all im brothers, all im sisters and all dem wey know am before come to am and eat bread with am for im house. Dem comfort am and cry with am about all di evil wey di Lord don bring on am. Each one give am one piece of money and one gold ring.
So di Lord bless di last part of Job life more than im beginning, and e get 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys.
E get seven sons and three daughters too.
E call di name of di first Jemimah, di name of di second Keziah and di name of di third Keren Happuch.
For all di land no women dey wey fine like Job daughters, and dem papa give dem inheritance among dem brothers.
After dis Job live 140 years and see im sons and im sons pikin dem, four generations.
So Job die, old and full of days.
